  [32:0:1.4] Adriatic (arm of the Mediterranean) | Italy, Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia (short Neum coast), Montenegro, Albania | North Macedonia (landlocked)
  [32:0:1.5] North Sea | UK, Norway, Denmark, Germany, Netherlands, Belgium, France | Finland, Russia
  [32:0:1.6] Baltic Sea (brackish, 9 states) | Denmark, Germany, Poland, Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia, Russia, Finland, Sweden | Norway
  [32:0:1.7] Yellow Sea | China, North Korea, South Korea | 
  [32:0:1.8] Dead Sea | Israel, Jordan, West Bank (Palestine) | Lebanon
[32:0:2] - **Mediterranean** separates **Europe and Africa** (Asia on its east); joins the Atlantic at Gibraltar.
[32:0:3] - **Turkiye** lies between the **Black Sea (north) and the Mediterranean (south)**; it does not touch the Caspian.
[32:0:4] - **Gaza Strip:** on the **Mediterranean**, between Egypt and Israel (Hamas-run since 2007).
[32:0:5] - **Black Sea:** inland sea between **south-eastern Europe, the Caucasus and Anatolia**; reaches the Mediterranean through the Bosphorus, Sea of Marmara and Dardanelles.
[32:0:6] # Seas and Islands in the Mediterranean
[32:0:7] - **Balearic Islands** (Mallorca, capital Palma) – Spain, **western Mediterranean**. **Malta** – island state in the **Mediterranean**, south of Sicily.
[32:0:8] - **Tyrrhenian Sea:** west of Italy, enclosed by **Italy, Sicily, Sardinia and Corsica**. Ligurian Sea lies north of Corsica; Adriatic east of Italy; Aegean between Greece and Turkiye.
[32:0:9] - **Coral Sea:** north-east of Australia (Great Barrier Reef).
[32:0:10] # Records and Special Seas
[32:0:11] TABLE head: Item | Fact
  [32:0:11.0] Dead Sea – lowest point on land | Shore about 430+ m below sea level and falling ~1 m a year; PMF gives ~420 m; the APPSC key used 1,385 ft (~422 m, an older figure)
  [32:0:11.1] Dead Sea – salinity | ~238–250‰, about 9.6 times the ocean; "dead" because it has no macroscopic aquatic life (only microbes)
  [32:0:11.2] Dead Sea – "dying" | Shrinking: Jordan River water diverted, evaporation ponds for mineral extraction (human activity)
  [32:0:11.3] Highest salinity overall | Lake Assal (Djibouti, ~348‰); Lake Van 330‰, Dead Sea 238‰, Great Salt Lake 220‰; Red Sea only ~40‰, Baltic ~7‰
  [32:0:11.4] Sargasso Sea | Only sea without land boundaries (North Atlantic, sargassum weed) – not the Yellow Sea
  [32:0:11.5] Largest / shallowest sea | Philippine Sea / Sea of Azov (~14 m)
  [32:0:11.6] Deeper seas | Bering (~4,000 m) deeper than Baltic, Dead Sea, Azov
  [32:0:11.7] Bermuda Triangle | Western North Atlantic (Florida–Bermuda–Puerto Rico) – planes and ships "vanished"
[32:0:12] - **Aral Sea:** shrank after the **Amu Darya and Syr Darya** were diverted for Soviet cotton irrigation (human activity) – the Black Sea and Lake Baikal have not dried up.
[32:0:13] - **Red Sea:** an **axial trough** (rift) between **Africa and Arabia**, part of the Great Rift system; no permanent river enters it; it is not associated with Europe.
[32:0:14] - **Volcanoes:** none in the **Baltic Sea** (away from plate margins); the Caribbean has volcanic islands, the Caspian mud volcanoes.
[32:0:15] - **West → east:** **Mediterranean, Black Sea, Caspian, Aral**.
[32:0:16] - **Landlocked states near these seas:** **Azerbaijan** touches only the Caspian (books treat it as not landlocked); **Laos** is the only landlocked country of SE Asia; doubly landlocked: **Uzbekistan, Liechtenstein**.
[32:0:17] - **North Natuna Sea:** **Indonesia** renamed the part of the South China Sea in its EEZ north of the Natuna Islands (2017).
[32:0:18] > Most-asked: Mediterranean borders (UPSC 2015, 2017 – Jordan, Iraq do not), sea–country pairs (UPSC 2004, 2019), North Sea count (UPSC 2024), Caspian borders, Balearic/Malta location, Dead Sea depth and salinity.

[32:1:9] # Great Rift Valley Lakes (APPSC 2024)
[32:1:10] - The rift forms a **chain of lakes**; most of the big ones are **freshwater** (Tanganyika, Malawi, Albert, Edward, Kivu), a few eastern ones are soda lakes.
[32:1:11] - **Lake Malawi** is at the **southern end**; Western (Albertine) branch: Tanganyika, Albert, Edward, Kivu; Eastern branch: Turkana, Naivasha.
[32:1:12] - **Lake Victoria** is **not in the rift**: it lies in a shallow **depression between the two branches**. Lake Malawi = Lake Nyasa; Victoria = Victoria Nyanza (different lakes).
[32:1:13] > Most-asked: Baikal (deepest/oldest ×7), largest lake / largest freshwater lake (Caspian vs Superior), Victoria as the Tanzania–Uganda boundary (UPSC 2000 ×3), Finland, lake–country pairs.

## SUB 2 | Rivers of Asia and Europe – Courses and Mouths
[32:2:0] # Asia
[32:2:1] - **Mekong** ("Danube of the East", ~4,900 km): Tibet → Yunnan (China), **Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam** → **South China Sea** – **not Malaysia, not Bangladesh**, not the Andaman Sea.
[32:2:2] - **Salween** flows **south** (Tibet → Myanmar → Andaman Sea); **Amur** flows north-east to the Sea of Okhotsk (Russia–China border); **Ob, Yenisei, Lena** flow **north** to the Arctic.
[32:2:3] - **Amu Darya and Syr Darya** → **Aral Sea**. **Tigris + Euphrates** → Shatt al-Arab → Persian Gulf (Tigris is in Asia; the **Niger** is African).
[32:2:4] - **Khorat (Siam) Plateau:** NE Thailand, between the **Menam (Chao Phraya) basin and the Mekong**. The Irrawaddy and Sittang are in Myanmar (Pegu Yoma between them).
[32:2:5] - River **Ma** – Bhutan; River **Po** – **Italy** (largest Italian river, into the Adriatic).
[32:2:6] # Europe

  [32:2:7.0] Volga | Valdai Hills | Caspian Sea | Longest in Europe; Volga–Don canal
  [32:2:7.1] Danube | Black Forest (Germany) | Black Sea (delta) | Second longest; most international (10 countries)
  [32:2:7.2] Dnieper | Valdai Hills | Black Sea | Russia, Belarus, Ukraine; Kyiv
  [32:2:7.3] Rhine | Swiss Alps | North Sea (Rotterdam) | Flows through a rift valley (Black Forest–Vosges); busiest inland waterway
  [32:2:7.4] Elbe | Czech Republic | North Sea | Hamburg
  [32:2:7.5] Thames | – | North Sea | not the Irish Sea
  [32:2:7.6] Ebro, Jucar (Spain) | – | Mediterranean | also Rhone, Po (Adriatic), Nile
[32:2:8] - **Into the Black Sea:** **Danube and Dnieper** (and Dniester, Don via Azov) – not the Volga or Ural (Caspian).
[32:2:9] - **Rhine:** the main **industrial artery of western/northern Germany** (Ruhr joins at Duisburg; ore and coal move by barge) and **Rotterdam**, Europe's largest port, is at its **mouth** – both statements true.
[32:2:10] - **Black Forest** mountains lie along the Rhine (east bank); Pyrenees, Apennines, Carpathians do not.

## SUB 4 | Rivers and Waterfalls of Africa and the Americas
[32:4:0] # Nile
[32:4:1] - **White Nile** from **Lake Victoria**; **Blue Nile** from **Lake Tana** (Ethiopia); they meet at **Khartoum**; mouth Mediterranean (arcuate delta).
[32:4:2] - **Basin (11):** Burundi, Rwanda, DR Congo, Tanzania, Kenya, Uganda, Ethiopia, Eritrea, South Sudan, Sudan, Egypt – **NOT Chad**.
[32:4:3] - **Exotic river:** rises in a humid region and crosses a desert without local tributaries – the **Nile** (also Indus, Colorado).
[32:4:4] - **Egypt = "Gift of the Nile"** (Herodotus): the Nile valley is a long **oasis** in the Sahara.
[32:4:5] - **South Sudan:** **landlocked**, main river the **White Nile**, capital **Juba** (not Akobo), mainly Christian.
[32:4:6] # Other African Rivers
[32:4:7] - **Congo:** Atlantic; equatorial basin = home of the **Pygmies** (Mbuti, Baka); basin holds the **world's largest tropical peatland** (Cuvette Centrale, ~29 billion t carbon ≈ 3 years of global fossil emissions; UNEP 2023).
[32:4:8] - **Zambezi:** **Victoria Falls** ("Mosi-oa-Tunya", the Smoke that Thunders; **Zambia–Zimbabwe** border, not Mozambique), **Kariba Dam**; into the **Indian Ocean**.
[32:4:9] - **Niger:** rises in Fouta Djallon; inland delta in Mali; "Oil River"; Gulf of Guinea. **Limpopo:** crosses the Tropic of Capricorn twice; Indian Ocean.
[32:4:10] # Americas
[32:4:11] - **Mississippi:** rises at glacial **Lake Itasca** (Minnesota); into the **Gulf of Mexico** near New Orleans (bird's-foot delta).
[32:4:12] - **Rio Grande:** forms the **USA (Texas)–Mexico** border (Rio Bravo del Norte in Mexico).
[32:4:13] - **Amazon:** rises in the Peruvian Andes → Atlantic; **St Lawrence** links the Great Lakes to the Atlantic; **Colorado:** Grand Canyon, Hoover Dam.
[32:4:14] # Waterfalls
[32:4:15] TABLE head: Fall | River / place | Note
  [32:4:15.0] Victoria | Zambezi, Zambia–Zimbabwe | Largest sheet of falling water
  [32:4:15.1] Angel | Churun, Venezuela | Highest (979 m)
  [32:4:15.2] Tugela | South Africa | Second highest
  [32:4:15.3] Iguazu | Argentina–Brazil | Largest fall system
  [32:4:15.4] Niagara | Niagara River, Lake Erie → Lake Ontario | USA–Canada
[32:4:16] > Most-asked: Victoria Falls on the Zambezi (×3), Congo peatland (UPSC 2024 ×2), Chad not in the Nile basin, Blue Nile/Lake Tana, Mississippi source and mouth.

  [32:8:0.10] Bass | – | Australia – Tasmania (not New Zealand)
  [32:8:0.11] Magellan / Drake Passage | Atlantic – Pacific | Magellan is the sheltered route; Drake is the stormiest, widest
[32:8:1] - Inland canals: **Volga–Don** (Russia), **Soo** (Superior–Huron), Welland (Erie–Ontario).
[32:8:2] ~~ Sources: PMF World Geography 04 p.43 (Panama Canal lock-based), 05 p.9 (White Sea–Baltic, Volga–Don canals); app notes 4:32 sub 7
[32:8:3] - **Lakes on the Suez Canal** (Port Said → Suez): Manzala, **Timsah**, **Great and Little Bitter Lakes**; **Gatun Lake** belongs to the **Panama** Canal.
[32:8:4] - **Ludwig Canal:** old inland waterway of **southern Germany (Bavaria)**, Danube–Main; succeeded by the **Rhine–Main–Danube Canal**.
[32:8:5] - **Malacca littoral states:** **Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore** (Thailand at the northern mouth).
## SUB 9 | Islands and Archipelagos
[32:9:0] TABLE head: Rank | Island | Note
  [32:9:0.0] 1 | Greenland | Denmark
  [32:9:0.1] 2 | New Guinea | Indonesia + PNG
  [32:9:0.2] 3 | Borneo | Largest in Asia; Kalimantan = Indonesian part; Malaysia, Brunei
  [32:9:0.3] 4 | Madagascar | Largest in the Indian Ocean
  [32:9:0.4] 5 | Baffin | Canada
[32:9:1] - **Japan** (N→S): Hokkaido, Honshu, Shikoku, Kyushu; **Shikoku** smallest; **Kanto** plain most extensive lowland.
[32:9:2] - **Indonesia:** **Java** most populous. **Svalbard** – **Norway** (India's **Himadri** station). **Socotra** – **Yemen**. **Normandy** – **France**. **Aleutians** – between **Alaska and Russia**. Faroe – "Sheep Islands"; Svalbard – "High Arctic Islands".
[32:9:3] - **Diego Garcia:** with **Mauritius** until 1965, then the UK. **Hong Kong** returned to China in **1997**. **Ireland** – "**Emerald Isle**". **Majuli** – largest river island of India (Brahmaputra). Norway's coast – **fjords**.
[32:9:4] ~~ Sources: PMF World Geography 01 p.12 (Major islands of Asia), 04 p.53 (islands of Europe); app notes 4:32 sub 8
[32:9:5] - **Grenada:** island nation in the **south-eastern Caribbean** ('Island of Spice').
[32:9:6] - **Senkaku / Diaoyu Islands:** uninhabited, **East China Sea**; Japan administers, **China** (and Taiwan) claim them (UPSC 2022).
[32:9:7] - **Indonesia W → E:** **Sumatra, Java, Bali, Lombok** (Lesser Sundas continue Sumbawa, Flores, Timor).
[32:9:8] - **Tribes and places:** **Koryak – Russian Far East** (not Alaska: Eskimo/Inuit); **Dayak – Borneo**; Bedouin – Arabian desert; **Lapp/Sami – Norway, Sweden, Finland**.
[32:9:9] - **Bougainville:** autonomous region of **Papua New Guinea**; voted ~98% for independence (Nov–Dec 2019, non-binding); PNG parliament still to ratify (as of 2026; target 2027–30).
[32:9:10] - **Hong Kong:** Kowloon **peninsula** + New Territories + Hong Kong Island and **~236 (now 260+) islands**; returned to China 1997.
[32:9:11] - **Mallorca** – Spain (Balearics); **Sardinia** – Italy; **Corsica** – France (UPSC 2025 pairs).
[32:9:12] - **Caribbean islands:** Grenada ('Island of Spice'), Montserrat, Anguilla (Lesser Antilles); **Madeira** and the Canaries are in the **Atlantic** off Africa.
[32:9:13] - **Honshu** – largest Japanese island (Tokyo); Hokkaido second.
[32:9:14] - **Socotra (Yemen):** UNESCO natural World Heritage Site (**2008**), dragon's blood trees.
[32:9:15] - **Kyushu:** southern main island of Japan – **Nagasaki** (A-bomb, 9 Aug 1945), Fukuoka; Hiroshima is on Honshu.
[32:9:16] - **Indonesia:** world's largest archipelago, **~17,500 islands** (14,000 in older books), from **Aceh** (Sumatra) to the **Torres Strait**; Philippines ~7,600.
[32:9:17] - **Most islands:** **Indonesia** (~17,500) > Philippines (~7,600) among the usual options; counting islets, **Sweden** (~2.2 lakh).
[32:9:18] - **Borneo:** shared by **Indonesia, Malaysia, Brunei**; a **tectonic (accreted) block on the Sunda Shelf, not volcanic** – unlike volcanic Java and Sumatra (UPPCS 2022).
[32:9:19] - **Galapagos:** **volcanic** hotspot islands of **Ecuador** (not Peru), Pacific.

=== NOTES 4:33 | India – Location, Extent, Frontiers, Standard Meridian and Neighbouring Countries
## SUB 0 | Land Neighbours, Border Lengths and Border States
[33:0:0] # Neighbours and border lengths (longest first)
[33:0:1] TABLE head: Rank | Country | Direction | Border (km) | Indian States / UTs on the border
  [33:0:1.0] 1 | Bangladesh | East | 4,096.7 (longest) | 5 States: West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram
  [33:0:1.1] 2 | China | North | 3,488 | Ladakh (UT), Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh
  [33:0:1.2] 3 | Pakistan | West | 3,323 | Gujarat, Rajasthan, Punjab, J&K (UT), Ladakh (UT)
  [33:0:1.3] 4 | Nepal | North | 1,751 | 5 States: Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, Sikkim
  [33:0:1.4] 5 | Myanmar | East | 1,643 | 4 States: Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram
  [33:0:1.5] 6 | Bhutan | North-east | 699 | 4 States: Sikkim, West Bengal, Assam, Arunachal Pradesh
  [33:0:1.6] 7 | Afghanistan | North-west | 106 (shortest) | Ladakh only (via PoK, Wakhan Corridor)
[33:0:2] - **Total land border: 15,106.7 km** with **7 countries**, through **92 districts of 16 States and 2 UTs**.
[33:0:3] - **Ascending order** of the big four: **Nepal < Pakistan < China < Bangladesh**; descending: Bangladesh > China > Pakistan > Nepal.
[33:0:4] - **Nine neighbours** in all: 7 by land + **Sri Lanka and Maldives**, which touch India **only by sea** (answer "two" when asked how many of the nine share only sea borders).
[33:0:5] - **SAARC** includes all of India's neighbours **except China** (and Myanmar); Afghanistan is a SAARC member but **not part of the Indian subcontinent** (Pakistan, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, India). **Maldives** = smallest South Asian country.

[33:0:8] - **Bhutan neighbours:** Sikkim, West Bengal, Assam, Arunachal Pradesh. **Nepal neighbours:** Sikkim, Bihar, Uttarakhand, UP, West Bengal. **Myanmar neighbours:** Arunachal, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram.
[33:0:9] - **Chicken's Neck:** the **Siliguri corridor** (West Bengal), ~20–22 km wide between Nepal and Bangladesh, links the **North-East with the rest of India**; Doklam (India–China–Bhutan tri-junction) lies close to it.
[33:0:10] - **Chumbi Valley:** a wedge of Tibet **between Sikkim and Bhutan** (reached by Nathu La and Jelep La).

## SUB 1 | Islands, Seas, Straits and Channels; India–Sri Lanka
[33:1:0] # Channels and straits around India
[33:1:1] TABLE head: Channel / strait | Separates or links
  [33:1:1.0] Ten Degree Channel (along 10° N, ~150 km) | Andaman group – Nicobar group
  [33:1:1.1] Nine Degree Channel | Minicoy – main Lakshadweep group
  [33:1:1.2] Eight Degree Channel | Minicoy (Lakshadweep) – Maldives
  [33:1:1.3] Palk Strait | Tamil Nadu – Sri Lanka (Jaffna); links Palk Bay (Bay of Bengal) with the Gulf of Mannar; named after Robert Palk, Governor of Madras (1763–67)
  [33:1:1.4] Duncan Passage | South Andaman – Little Andaman
[33:1:2] - **India and Sri Lanka** are separated by the **Palk Strait and the Gulf of Mannar**; one-word answer = **Palk Strait**. The **Gulf of Mannar** lies **south-east of Tamil Nadu** (between SE India and western Sri Lanka), south of Adam's Bridge.
[33:1:3] - From **Nagercoil/Kanyakumari** (south of Adam's Bridge) the sea route to Sri Lanka crosses the **Gulf of Mannar**; the Palk Strait lies farther north (Rameswaram–Point Calimere to Jaffna).
[33:1:4] - **Palk Bay** lies between the **Gulf of Mannar and the Bay of Bengal** (bounded in the south by Adam's Bridge).
[33:1:5] - **Adam's Bridge (Rama Setu):** a chain of **limestone shoals** between **Dhanushkodi (Pamban Island) and Talaimannar** (~32 km).
[33:1:6] - **Sethusamudram Project:** a proposed 167 km shipping channel linking the **Gulf of Mannar with Palk Bay**.
[33:1:7] # Island groups
[33:1:8] TABLE head: Item | Andaman & Nicobar | Lakshadweep
  [33:1:8.0] Sea | Bay of Bengal (Andaman Sea to the east) | Arabian Sea (Laccadive Sea), off the Malabar coast of Kerala
  [33:1:8.1] Origin | Tectonic / submarine mountains; Barren Island = India's only active volcano | Coral islands (atolls)
  [33:1:8.2] Number | ~572 islands/islets (NCERT); the Andaman group alone "about 200" (PMF) – the usual exam key | 36 islands
  [33:1:8.3] Capital | Port Blair (South Andaman) | Kavaratti
  [33:1:8.4] Southern tip / largest | Great Nicobar – Indira Point | Minicoy (southernmost and largest)
[33:1:9] - **Port Blair** is nearer by sea to **Yangon (Myanmar)** than to Kolkata, Chennai or Machilipatnam.
[33:1:10] - **Sea neighbours of the A&N Islands:** Myanmar, Thailand, Indonesia (not Sri Lanka). Water bodies: Arabian Sea (west), Bay of Bengal (east), Indian Ocean (south), Lakshadweep Sea (south-west).
[33:1:11] ~~ Sources: NextGen Indian Geography - APPSC Exams 06 p.3-5; PMF Indian Physical Geography 01 p.22; PMF Indian Physical Geography 02 p.9-13; OnlyIAS NCERT Indian Geography 03 p.18; Rocket Indian Geography p.18, p.84; app notes 4:33 sub 6-7
[33:1:12] - **Lakshadweep:** formerly the **Laccadive, Minicoy and Amindivi** islands, renamed **1973**; lies off the **Malabar** (not Coromandel) coast.

## SUB 3 | Boundary Lines and Disputed Tracts
[33:3:0] TABLE head: Line | Between | Year | Note
  [33:3:0.0] Radcliffe Line | India–Pakistan (and India–Bangladesh) | 1947 | Sir Cyril Radcliffe; Partition award
  [33:3:0.1] McMahon Line | India–China (Arunachal Pradesh–Tibet) | 1914 | Sir Henry McMahon; Simla (Shimla) Convention; east of Nepal; China rejects it
  [33:3:0.2] Durand Line | British India–Afghanistan (now Pakistan–Afghanistan) | 1893 | Sir Mortimer Durand; Durand Mission fixed the Afghan border, buffer against Russia
  [33:3:0.3] Line of Control | India–Pakistan (J&K) | 1972 | 1948–49 ceasefire line renamed under the Simla Agreement (1972, India–Pakistan)
  [33:3:0.4] Line of Actual Control | India–China | Post-1962 | De facto; western (Ladakh), middle (HP, Uttarakhand), eastern (Sikkim, Arunachal) sectors
  [33:3:0.5] Johnson Line / McDonald Line | Aksai Chin | 1865 / 1893 | Johnson = India's claim; McDonald = China's
  [33:3:0.6] Maginot Line | France–Germany | – | Not an Indian line
[33:3:1] - **Shaksgam Valley:** part of PoK (Gilgit-Baltistan), **5,180 sq km ceded by Pakistan to China in 1963**; India protests Chinese construction there.
[33:3:2] - **Sir Creek:** **India–Pakistan** dispute; ~96 km tidal estuary in the Rann of Kutch between **Gujarat and Sindh**.
[33:3:3] - **India–Pakistan boundary = superimposed boundary** (drawn by an outside power across a settled cultural landscape).
[33:3:4] - **Rivers as international borders (world):** **Rio Grande (USA–Mexico)**; the Rhine also forms the Swiss–German and French–German borders; the Indus and Nile do not form borders.

## SUB 5 | Tropic of Cancer and the Standard Meridian
[33:5:0] - **Tropic of Cancer (23°30′ N)** passes through **8 States**, west to east: **Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, Mizoram**; it roughly halves India. **Andhra Pradesh lies wholly south** of it; it does not touch Odisha or Bihar.
[33:5:1] - **Indian Standard Meridian: 82°30′ E** (a multiple of 7°30′), reference place **Mirzapur (UP)**; **IST = GMT/UTC + 5:30**.
[33:5:2] - It passes through **5 States:** **Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh** (not Telangana). **Chhattisgarh** lies on both the Tropic and the meridian; **Odisha** only on the meridian.
[33:5:3] - **Time spread:** ~30° of longitude = **~2 hours** (1° = 4 min); the sun rises in the North-East about 2 hours before Jaisalmer.
[33:5:4] - **Separate time zone demand:** **Arunachal Pradesh** CM Pema Khandu (2017) asked for a North-East time zone; India keeps a single zone.
[33:5:5] ~~ Sources: Rocket Indian Geography p.116, p.118-120; PMF Indian Physical Geography 01 p.13-14; app notes 4:33 sub 1-2

=== NOTES 4:34 | India – Physiographic Division: the Himalayas (ranges, Regional Divisions, Passes)
## SUB 0 | Parallel Ranges – Himadri, Himachal, Shiwalik and the Trans-Himalaya
[34:0:0] # The three parallel (longitudinal) ranges
[34:0:1] TABLE head: Feature | Himadri (Greater / Inner / Central) | Himachal (Lesser / Middle) | Shiwalik (Outer / foothills)
  [34:0:1.0] Position | Northernmost of the three | Between Himadri and Shiwalik | Outermost, southernmost
  [34:0:1.1] Age | Oldest | Intermediate | Youngest (Pliocene, Cenozoic era)
  [34:0:1.2] Height | Average 6,000 m; loftiest peaks | 3,500–4,500 m (avg ~4,000 m) | 900–1,100 m
  [34:0:1.3] Width | 160–400 km (NCERT summary; PMF) | ~50 km | 10–50 km, narrowest
  [34:0:1.4] Make-up | Granite core (central crystallines); asymmetrical folds | Highly compressed and altered rocks; most rugged system | Unconsolidated river sediments; simple Jura-type folds
  [34:0:1.5] Continuity | Most continuous range | Broken into ranges | Continuous to the Gandak, then broken
  [34:0:1.6] Known for | Everest, Kanchenjunga, Nanda Devi, Kamet; long glaciers | Pir Panjal, Dhauladhar, Mussoorie, Nag Tibba, Mahabharat (Nepal); Kashmir, Kangra, Kullu valleys; hill stations | Foothills; duns behind them; debris built the plains
[34:0:2] - **Three parallel ranges** in the longitudinal extent: **Himadri, Himachal, Shiwalik** (NCERT) – a statement "four parallel ranges" is false; "the northernmost range is the Shiwalik" is false (northernmost = **Himadri**).
[34:0:3] - **Himadri:** also called Greater, Higher, Inner or **Central** Himalaya; highest point **Mount Everest** (~8,850 m; now 8,848.86 m). Dehradun is **not** in the Himadri (it is a dun between Lesser Himalaya and Shiwalik).
[34:0:4] - **Himachal:** names for the same range – Lesser, Middle, Lower Himalaya; "Himachal stands for the Middle Himalaya".
[34:0:5] - **Pir Panjal:** the most important Lesser Himalayan range, **~300 km from the Jhelum to the upper Beas** in **J&K and Himachal Pradesh**; Banihal pass crosses it. South-east of the Ravi it continues as the **Dhauladhar**, then the **Mussoorie** range (Uttarakhand) and the **Mahabharat Lekh** in **Nepal**.
[34:0:6] - **Shiwalik:** formed from riverine deposits of the "Siwalik river" (Pascoe, Pilgrim) about **2–5 million years ago** (Pliocene, **Cenozoic**); local names – **Jammu Hills** (J&K), **Dhang/Dundwa** (Uttarakhand), **Churia Ghat** (Nepal).
[34:0:7] - **Youngest mountain chain** among Vindhyas, Aravalli, Shiwaliks, Annamalai = **Shiwaliks**; **oldest Himalayan range** = **Greater Himalaya**.
[34:0:8] - **In Arunachal Pradesh** the Lesser/outer Himalayan hills are the **Dafla, Miri, Abor and Mishmi hills** (PMF lists them as Lesser Himalaya; the Shiwalik is almost absent there).
[34:0:9] # The Trans-Himalaya (Tibetan Himalaya)
[34:0:10] - Lies **north of the Himadri**; mostly in Tibet, hence the **Tibet Himalaya**; **formed before** the Himalayas.
[34:0:11] - Ranges: **Karakoram** (K2), **Ladakh** (continues into Tibet as the **Kailash Range**, not the Zaskar), **Zaskar** (Kashmir Valley separates the Pir Panjal from it), **Kailash** (Mt Kailash 6,714 m; **Lake Manasarovar** lies near it in Tibet).
[34:0:12] - **Ladakh Plateau:** north-east of the Karakoram; **highest plateau in India**; includes the **Aksai Chin**, Soda Plains, Lingzi Tang, Depsang Plains (Chinese-occupied Aksai Chin is a cold desert).
[34:0:13] - **Kailash Mansarovar** is in **Chinese Tibet** – Indian pilgrims need a visa.
[34:0:14] # Sequence questions (north ↔ south)
[34:0:15] TABLE head: Asked | Answer
  [34:0:15.0] N → S (all) | Karakoram – Ladakh – Zaskar – Pir Panjal – Shiwalik
  [34:0:15.1] N → S (four) | Karakoram – Ladakh – Zanskar – Shiwalik
  [34:0:15.2] N → S (main) | Karakoram – Himadri – Himachal – Shiwalik
  [34:0:15.3] S → N (west) | Shiwalik – Lesser Himalaya – Great Himalaya
  [34:0:15.4] Northward | Pir Panjal – Zanskar – Ladakh – Karakoram
  [34:0:15.5] S → N | Dhauladhar – Zanskar – Ladakh – Karakoram
  [34:0:15.6] Hills S → N | Satmala (Maharashtra) – Kaimur (MP–UP–Bihar) – Naga (Nagaland) – Pir Panjal (J&K–HP)
[34:0:16] - The **Lesser Himalaya lies between the Shiwalik and the Great Himalaya**.
[34:0:17] > Statement trap (APPSC 2023): "Shiwaliks are composed of highly compressed and altered rocks" ✗ (that is the Himachal); "folds of the Great Himalaya are symmetrical" ✗; "Himadri is the most continuous range, average 6,000 m" ✓.
[34:0:18] ~~ Sources: NextGen Indian Geography - APPSC Exams 04 p.8-11; OnlyIAS NCERT Indian Geography 03 p.13; PMF Indian Physical Geography 01 p.38-44, p.52; app notes 4:34 (sub 2)
[34:0:19] - **Northern mountains = three divisions:** the **Himalayas**, the **Trans-Himalayas** and the **Purvanchal** (eastern hills); Himadri, Himachal and Shiwalik are the parallel ranges of the Himalayas.
## SUB 1 | Peaks and Mountaineering
[34:1:0] # Heights and location
[34:1:1] TABLE head: Peak | Height | Range / division | Location
  [34:1:1.0] Mount Everest | 8,848 m (2020 survey: 8,848.86 m) | Himadri; Central (Nepal) Himalaya | Nepal–China (Tibet) border; highest on Earth; Sagarmatha (Nepal), Qomolangma (Tibet)
  [34:1:1.1] K2 (Godwin Austen, Qogir) | 8,611 m | Karakoram (Trans-Himalaya) | Gilgit-Baltistan (Indian claim, PoK); world's 2nd; "highest in the Indian Union" (NextGen, PMF)
  [34:1:1.2] Kanchenjunga | 8,586 m (older 8,598 m) | Himadri | Sikkim–Nepal border; world's 3rd; highest under Indian control
  [34:1:1.3] Lhotse / Makalu | 8,516 / 8,485 m | Himadri | Nepal–China
  [34:1:1.4] Cho Oyu | 8,188 m (older estimate 8,153 m) | Himadri | Nepal–Tibet; world's 6th
  [34:1:1.5] Nanga Parbat | 8,126 m | Western end of the Himalaya (Zaskar/Punjab Himalaya) | PoK; "Naked Mountain"
  [34:1:1.6] Nanda Devi | 7,817 m | Himadri; Kumaon Himalaya | Uttarakhand (Chamoli, Garhwal division); highest wholly in India
  [34:1:1.7] Kamet, Trishul | 7,756 m, — | Himadri, Kumaon | Uttarakhand
  [34:1:1.8] Namcha Barwa | 7,755 m | Eastern end; Assam / Arunachal Himalaya | Tibet, at the Brahmaputra bend
  [34:1:1.9] Mt Kailash | 6,714 m | Kailash Range (Trans-Himalaya) | Tibet
  [34:1:1.10] Gosainthan (Shishapangma) | 8,027 m | Himalaya | Tibet – not in India
[34:1:2] - **Highest peak of India:** **K2 (Godwin Austen)** in the Indian claim (NextGen, PMF); **Kanchenjunga** is the highest in Indian-administered territory (Rocket) – papers key either; with K2 offered, answer K2; without it, Kanchenjunga.
[34:1:3] - **Nanda Devi:** 4th highest in India (after K2, Kanchenjunga, Nanga Parbat; PMF calls it 2nd after Kangchenjunga, counting only Indian-held peaks); part of the **Kumaon Himalaya** (UPSC 2003); Nanda Devi NP = UNESCO site (1988).
[34:1:4] - **Descending height:** Everest – Godwin Austen – Kanchenjunga.
[34:1:5] - **Cho Oyu and Lhotse** are Himalayan; **Annamalai and Sirumalai** are Tamil Nadu hills.
[34:1:6] # East-to-west orders
[34:1:7] - **Namcha Barwa – Kanchenjunga – Everest – Nanda Devi** (Rocket "east → west").
[34:1:8] - **Kanchenjunga – Everest – Annapurna – Dhaulagiri**.
[34:1:9] - **Garo Hills – Nanda Devi – Kamet – K2**.
[34:1:10] # Mountaineering firsts
[34:1:11] - **First woman on Everest:** **Junko Tabei** (Japan, 1975).
[34:1:12] - **First woman to climb Everest twice:** **Santosh Yadav** (India, 1992 and 1993).
[34:1:13] # Mountain systems matched
[34:1:14] TABLE head: Range | Fact
  [34:1:14.0] Aravalli | Guru Shikhar 1,722 m
  [34:1:14.1] Satpura and Vindhya | Dhupgarh 1,350 m (Satpura); Kalumar peak (Vindhya)
  [34:1:14.2] Himalaya | Nanga Parbat (west) to Namcha Barwa (east)
  [34:1:14.3] Karakoram and Pir Panjal (Kashmir Himalaya) | Siachen and Biafo glaciers
  [34:1:14.4] Kanchenjunga / Dhauladhar / Karakoram | Greater / Middle / Trans-Himalaya
[34:1:15] ~~ Sources: NextGen Indian Geography - APPSC Exams 04 p.9, p.11; PMF Indian Physical Geography 01 p.40, p.42, p.51-52; Rocket Indian Geography p.36, p.38, p.103; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cho_Oyu; app notes 4:34 (sub 5)

  [34:2:1.15] Arunachal | Bum La | 4,600 m | Tawang–Tibet
  [34:2:1.16] Arunachal | Diphu, Pangsau | — | India–Myanmar
[34:2:2] - **West → east:** **Banihal – Mana – Nathu La – Bum La**; Zoji La – Shipki La – Lipulekh – Nathu La.
[34:2:3] - **Highest of Zoji La, Rohtang, Nathu La, Khyber:** **Nathu La** (4,310 m > Rohtang 3,978 m > Zoji La 3,528 m > Khyber).
[34:2:4] - **Wrong pair (UPPSC 2025):** Lipulekh is in **Uttarakhand**, not Ladakh; Nathu La – Sikkim, Bomdila – Arunachal, Shipki La – Himachal are right.
[34:2:5] # Nathu La timeline
[34:2:6] - **2006:** reopened for **India–China border trade** (closed since 1962).
[34:2:7] - **Sept 2014:** India–China agreement – new **Kailash-Mansarovar** route via **Nathu La**.
[34:2:8] - **2017:** China halted the pilgrims via Nathu La (Doklam standoff); Lipulekh route continued.
[34:2:9] # Tunnels
[34:2:10] TABLE head: Tunnel | Pass / route
  [34:2:10.0] Atal Tunnel (9.02 km) | Under Rohtang; Manali – Lahaul-Spiti
  [34:2:10.1] Jawahar Tunnel | Banihal, Jammu–Srinagar
  [34:2:10.2] Zoji-la Tunnel | Srinagar–Leh
[34:2:11] ~~ Sources: PMF Indian Physical Geography 01 p.48, p.66-70; NextGen Indian Geography - APPSC Exams 04 p.9; newsonair.gov.in (Mig La, 5 Oct 2025); app notes 4:34 (sub 7)
[34:2:12] - **Tuju pass** (Manipur): **Imphal – Tamu (Myanmar)**.
[34:2:13] - **Avalanche-prone passes:** **Zoji La, Khardung La, Rohtang, Mana**.
[34:2:14] - **Yang Yap pass** (Arunachal): the **Brahmaputra enters India** near it.
[34:2:15] - **Peninsular passes:** **Thalghat and Bhor Ghat** (Maharashtra, Western Ghats); **Palghat Gap** (Kerala).
## SUB 3 | Purvanchal and the North-eastern Hills
[34:3:0] # Purvanchal
[34:3:1] - Beyond the **Dihang gorge** (near Namcha Barwa) the Himalaya takes a knee-bend and turns south as the **Purvanchal** – "eastern offshoots of the Himalayas", 500–3,000 m; Arunachal, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura, eastern Assam.
[34:3:2] - **Latest in origin** among Ajanta, Palkonda, Kaimur, Patkai = **Patkai** (Tertiary, Himalayan).
[34:3:3] TABLE head: Hills | State / fact
  [34:3:3.0] Patkai Bum | Arunachal Pradesh – Myanmar border; with the Naga Hills forms the India–Myanmar watershed; touches Arunachal, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram – not Tripura
  [34:3:3.1] Naga Hills | Nagaland; Saramati 3,826 m
  [34:3:3.2] Manipur Hills | Manipur; Loktak lake; Manipur is mostly mountainous
  [34:3:3.3] Barail Range | Assam; separates Manipur from Nagaland, links Naga and Mizo hills; highest range of Assam
  [34:3:3.4] Mizo (Lushai) Hills | Mizoram; Blue Mountain; run north–south; Molasse basin (soft, unconsolidated deposits)
  [34:3:3.5] Garo, Khasi, Jaintia | Meghalaya (Shillong Plateau) – part of the Purvanchal/eastern hills group; Nokrek 1,412 m in the Garo Hills
  [34:3:3.6] Bhuban Hills | Assam (Barak valley) – not in the Meghalaya Plateau
  [34:3:3.7] Miri Hills | Arunachal Pradesh – not Meghalaya
  [34:3:3.8] Arakan Yoma | Myanmar – southern extension of the Himalaya/Purvanchal; highest Natma Taung (Mt Victoria)
[34:3:4] - **West → east:** **Garo – Khasi – Jaintia – Naga**.
[34:3:5] - **Shillong** and **Cherrapunji (Sohra)** are on the **Khasi Hills**; Shillong = "Scotland of the East".
[34:3:6] - **India–Myanmar boundary ranges:** Patkai, Naga, Mizo (Lushai) hills – a "Khasi, Patkai and Arakan Yoma" option is wrong (Khasi is in Meghalaya, Arakan wholly in Myanmar).
[34:3:7] - **Mountains on India's eastern border with Myanmar:** **Patkai**.
[34:3:8] ~~ Sources: NextGen Indian Geography - APPSC Exams 04 p.11-12; PMF Indian Physical Geography 01 p.46-47, p.86; Rocket Indian Geography p.19, p.42; app notes 4:34 (sub 8)
## SUB 4 | Valleys, Duns, Karewas and Hill Stations
[34:4:0] # Valleys
[34:4:1] TABLE head: Valley | Location
  [34:4:1.0] Kashmir Valley | In the Himachal (Lesser Himalaya) zone, between the Great Himalaya (Himadri) (NE) and the Pir Panjal (SW)
  [34:4:1.1] Kullu Valley | Himachal Pradesh, between the Dhauladhar and Pir Panjal
  [34:4:1.2] Kashmir, Kangra, Kullu | The famous valleys of the Himachal range
  [34:4:1.3] Markha / Dzukou / Sangla / Yumthang | Ladakh (J&K at the time) / Nagaland / Himachal / Sikkim
  [34:4:1.4] Nelang Valley | Uttarakhand (Gangotri NP, Uttarkashi), near the China border
  [34:4:1.5] Valley of Flowers | Himachal–Uttarakhand Himalaya (Uttarakhand)
  [34:4:1.6] Kathmandu, Pokhara | Nepal, between Great and Lesser Himalaya
[34:4:2] # Duns
[34:4:3] - **Duns (Doons):** **longitudinal valleys between the Lesser Himalaya and the Shiwalik** (NCERT) – not between Greater and Lesser; called **duars** in the east.
[34:4:4] - Examples: **Dehra Dun (largest)**, Kotli Dun, Patli Dun, Nalagarh Dun – "Nalagarh is the largest dun" is false.
[34:4:5] - "The valleys in the Siwalik ranges are called" = **Duns**.
[34:4:6] # Karewas
[34:4:7] - **Karewas:** thick lake (lacustrine) and glacial-clay deposits forming flat-topped terraces in the **Kashmir Himalaya**; soils used for **zafran (saffron)**.
[34:4:8] - The **Kashmir valley** produces the largest quantity of saffron in India.
[34:4:9] # People
[34:4:10] - **Dogras** live mainly from the **southern Pir Panjal region to the Punjab plains** (Jammu region).
[34:4:11] # Hill stations
[34:4:12] TABLE head: Hill station | State
  [34:4:12.0] Manali | Himachal Pradesh
  [34:4:12.1] Mussoorie, Champawat | Uttarakhand
  [34:4:12.2] Coorg (Kodagu) | Karnataka
  [34:4:12.3] Ooty, Kodaikanal | Tamil Nadu
  [34:4:12.4] Munnar | Kerala
  [34:4:12.5] Kurseong | West Bengal
[34:4:13] - Most Himalayan hill stations (Shimla, Mussoorie, Ranikhet, Nainital, Almora, Darjeeling) lie in the **Middle Himalaya**.
[34:4:14] ~~ Sources: OnlyIAS NCERT Indian Geography 03 p.13; PMF Indian Physical Geography 01 p.43-44, p.48-50, p.53-54; NextGen Indian Geography - APPSC Exams 04 p.10; Rocket Indian Geography p.90; app notes 4:34 (sub 3)
[34:4:15] - **Karewas** are locally called **Vuhr**.
## SUB 5 | Dimensions, Origin, Structure and Significance
[34:5:0] # Dimensions
[34:5:1] TABLE head: Dimension | Figure
  [34:5:1.0] Length | ~2,400 km (2,414 km) – Nanga Parbat (west) to Namcha Barwa (east)
  [34:5:1.1] Width | 500 km (Kashmir) → 200 km (Arunachal) (NextGen); NCERT/PMF: 400 km → 150 km
  [34:5:1.2] Area | About 5 lakh sq km (not 15 lakh)
  [34:5:1.3] Eastern limit | The Brahmaputra (Dihang gorge) marks the eastern boundary
[34:5:2] - The Himalayas form the **northern boundary**, separating the subcontinent from the rest of Asia (not the Aravalli or the Ghats).
[34:5:3] - **Indian Himalayan Region:** HP, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, Arunachal, NE States, J&K, Ladakh and hill WB – **not Uttar Pradesh**.
[34:5:4] # Origin and structure
[34:5:5] - **Young fold mountains** of tectonic origin, raised from **Tethys (geosynclinal)** sediments in the **Tertiary** (Eocene–Pliocene) as the **Indian plate** pushed into Eurasia (~70 million years ago, still rising).
[34:5:6] - **Geologically young and unstable** landmass of India.
[34:5:7] - **Trans-Himalayas formed before** the Himalayas.
[34:5:8] - Folds of the **Himadri are asymmetrical** with a **granite** core; **steep slope faces the plains**, gentle slope faces Tibet.
[34:5:9] - **Structural zones (N → S):** Indus–Tsangpo Suture Zone (separates Himalaya from **Tibet**) → Main Central Thrust → Main Boundary Thrust → **Himalayan Frontal Fault** (separates Himalaya from the **plains**, not from Tibet).
[34:5:10] - **Antecedent drainage:** the Indus and Sutlej are older than the Himalaya and cut gorges through it.
[34:5:11] - **Fossils (UPPSC 2019 key):** Greater Himalaya sedimentary rocks fossil-less; marine fossils in the Lesser Himalaya; remains of human civilisation in the Shiwaliks.
[34:5:12] # Significance (IAS 2010: all three true)
[34:5:13] - Blocks **Siberian cold waves**; shapes the **monsoon** pattern; rivers and Shiwalik debris built the **Indo-Gangetic Plain's alluvium**.
[34:5:14] - **Plains** are the largest relief division of India (~43% of area).
[34:5:15] ~~ Sources: NextGen Indian Geography - APPSC Exams 04 p.8; PMF Indian Physical Geography 01 p.38, p.70; OnlyIAS NCERT Indian Geography 03 p.13-14; app notes 4:34 (sub 0)
## SUB 6 | Regional Divisions
[34:6:0] # Burrard's river-valley divisions (west → east)
[34:6:1] TABLE head: Division | Between rivers | Features
  [34:6:1.0] Punjab (Kashmir/Himachal) Himalaya | Indus – Sutlej | Nanga Parbat, Rakaposhi, Haramosh
  [34:6:1.1] Kumaon Himalaya | Sutlej – Kali | Uttarakhand; Nanda Devi, Trisul, Kamet; Milam, Pindari glaciers
  [34:6:1.2] Nepal (Central) Himalaya | Kali – Teesta | Everest, Kanchenjunga, Makalu, Dhaulagiri, Annapurna
  [34:6:1.3] Assam (Eastern) Himalaya | Teesta – Dihang (Brahmaputra) | Ends at the Namcha Barwa knee-bend
[34:6:2] - **Four** regional divisions (Burrard); NCERT's relief-based scheme has **five**: Kashmir (NW) Himalaya; Himachal–Uttarakhand Himalaya; Darjeeling–Sikkim Himalaya; Arunachal Himalaya; **Eastern hills and mountains**.
[34:6:3] - **Arunachal Himalaya:** east of Bhutan to the Diphu pass; peaks **Kangtu and Namcha Barwa**.
[34:6:4] - **Namcha Barwa** is **not** Garhwal Himalaya; **Nokrek** is in the Garo Hills, **not** Sikkim Himalaya.
[34:6:5] ~~ Sources: OnlyIAS NCERT Indian Geography 03 p.13; PMF Indian Physical Geography 01 p.48-52; app notes 4:34 (sub 4)
## SUB 7 | Glaciers
[34:7:0] TABLE head: Glacier | Range | Location / river
  [34:7:0.0] Siachen | Karakoram | Ladakh; north of the Nubra Valley; feeds the Nubra; largest glacier of India
  [34:7:0.1] Baltoro, Biafo, Hispar | Karakoram | Gilgit-Baltistan (PoK)
  [34:7:0.2] Gangotri | Greater Himalaya | Uttarkashi; Gomukh – source of the Bhagirathi
  [34:7:0.3] Bandarpunch | Greater Himalaya | Uttarkashi – Yamuna
  [34:7:0.4] Bara Shigri | Greater Himalaya | Lahaul, HP – Chenab; largest in HP
  [34:7:0.5] Milam | Kumaon | Source of the Gori Ganga (not the Mandakini)
  [34:7:0.6] Zemu | Sikkim | Largest of the Eastern Himalaya – Teesta (not the Manas)
[34:7:1] - **Largest among options:** **Siachen** (> Baltoro, Biafo, Chogo Lungma; > Gangotri, Zemu, Sasaini).
[34:7:2] - **Himalayan glaciers** are melting fast – the exam key says the **highest rate in the world**; Gangotri has shrunk to about half its extent in 50 years.
[34:7:3] ~~ Sources: PMF Indian Physical Geography 01 p.48, p.56-63; NextGen Indian Geography - APPSC Exams 04 p.9; app notes 4:34 (sub 6)
[34:7:4] - **Longest (decreasing):** **Hispar > Biafo > Drang Drung > Sonapani > Bara Shigri**.
[34:7:5] - **Kumaon glaciers:** **Pindari, Milam and Kafni**.

=== NOTES 4:35 | India – the Northern Plains, the Peninsular Plateau, the Coastal Plains and the Islands
## SUB 0 | Western and Eastern Ghats and the Southern Hills
[35:0:0] # Western Ghats vs Eastern Ghats
[35:0:1] TABLE head: Feature | Western Ghats (Sahyadri) | Eastern Ghats
  [35:0:1.0] Extent | Tapti valley to near Kanyakumari, about 1,600 km | Mahanadi (Odisha) to the Vaigai (Tamil Nadu), about 1,750 km
  [35:0:1.1] Continuity | Continuous; steep west face, gentle east slope; watershed of the Peninsula | Discontinuous, eroded groups of hills; cut by the Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri (not the Narmada)
  [35:0:1.2] Height | 900–1,600 m; rises from north to south (higher in the south) | Average about 600 m (610 m)
  [35:0:1.3] Rocks | Deccan lava in the north (horizontal sheets → stepped, "landing stair" look) | Khondalite and charnockite
  [35:0:1.4] Highest | Anamudi 2,695 m (Anaimalai, Kerala) = highest in South India and in the Peninsula | Jindhagada 1,690 m (PMF, Rocket) / Arma Konda 1,680 m = highest peak of Andhra Pradesh (Rocket); Mahendragiri ~1,501 m (Odisha)
  [35:0:1.5] Passes / gaps | Thal Ghat (Mumbai–Nashik), Bhor Ghat (Mumbai–Pune), Pal Ghat | River gaps
[35:0:2] - **"Ghat"** in Hindi means both **river-landing steps (stairs)** and a **mountain pass**; the WBCS 2017 key gives **"gap or pass"**.
[35:0:3] - **Local names, north → south:** **Sahyadri** (Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka) → **Nilgiri** → **Anaimalai** → Palani → **Cardamom (Yela Mala)**.
[35:0:4] - Sahyadri peaks: **Kalsubai (1,646 m, Maharashtra)**, Salher, Mahabaleshwar; **Mullayanagiri 1,892 m = highest of Karnataka** (Baba Budan hills).
[35:0:5] - A statement "the Western Ghats are higher in their northern region" is **false**; the Narmada and Tapi valleys are old rift valleys and the Tapi lies south of the Satpura.
[35:0:6] - **Vandaravu (Palani), Perumal Malai (Palani), Velliangiri (Coimbatore) and Anamudi** are peaks/hills of the **Western Ghats**.
[35:0:7] - Goran Ghat is **not** a Western Ghats pass.
[35:0:8] # Nilgiris – where the two Ghats meet
[35:0:9] - The **Eastern and Western Ghats meet at the Nilgiri Hills** (Gudalur), the **tri-junction of Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu**; "Blue Mountains".
[35:0:10] - **Doddabetta (2,637 m)** = highest of the Nilgiris, second in South India; **Ooty** lies in the Nilgiris; home of the **Toda** tribe.
[35:0:11] - **Pal Ghat (Palakkad gap)** at the southern end of the Nilgiris, **between the Nilgiris (north) and the Anaimalai (south)**; 144 m, about 24–30 km wide; misfit river Ponnani; Kerala–TN rail and road link.
[35:0:12] # Hills of the far south
[35:0:13] TABLE head: Hills | Place | Fact
  [35:0:13.0] Anaimalai | Kerala–TN | Anamudi; three ranges radiate from it
  [35:0:13.1] Palani (Palni) | Dindigul, TN | Kodaikanal
  [35:0:13.2] Cardamom (Yela Mala) | Kerala–Tamil Nadu border | Southernmost range; closest to Kanyakumari; Agastyamalai; tea at Kanan Devan (Munnar)
  [35:0:13.3] Shevaroy (Servarayan) | Salem, Tamil Nadu (Eastern Ghats) | Yercaud
  [35:0:13.4] Javadi, Biligirirangan | TN / Karnataka | Eastern Ghats remnants
  [35:0:13.5] Seshachalam | Southern Andhra Pradesh (Eastern Ghats, Tirupati) | Not part of the Western Ghats or Nilgiri/Palani
[35:0:14] - **Tea** grows in Kanan Devan, the Nilgiris and Darjeeling; **Girnar** (Gujarat) has **no tea**.
[35:0:15] - **UPSC 2023:** none of the three statements is correct – Amarkantak joins the **Vindhya and Satpura** (not Sahyadri); Biligirirangan is in **Karnataka** (Eastern Ghats, not Satpura); Seshachalam is in **Andhra Pradesh** (Eastern Ghats, not the southernmost Western Ghats).
[35:0:16] - **Eastern Ghats in AP:** Nallamala (Chenchus; **Srisailam Tiger Reserve**), Erramala (Krishna–Penna divide), Seshachalam (**red sanders**), Velikonda, Palkonda (Tirupati), **Papikondalu** (Godavari gorge); Araku Valley = "**Ooty of Andhra Pradesh**".
[35:0:17] > Exam angle: the Nilgiri "meeting point" is asked again and again (UPSC 2008, UPPSC, CGPSC 2024, MPPSC 2025); Anamudi vs Doddabetta is the classic trap.
[35:0:18] ~~ Sources: NextGen Indian Geography - APPSC Exams 05 p.12-14; PMF Indian Physical Geography 01 p.82-84; OnlyIAS NCERT Indian Geography 03 p.16; Rocket Indian Geography p.103; testbook.com (WBCS 2017 "ghat"); app notes 4:35 (sub 5, 6)
## SUB 1 | Peninsular Plateau – Structure, Plateaus and the Deccan Traps
[35:1:0] # Structure
[35:1:1] - **Oldest and largest** physiographic division; a **Precambrian shield**, part of **Gondwana land**; one of the most **stable** blocks; **not** of volcanic origin overall; rich in **metallic minerals**.
[35:1:2] - About **16 lakh sq km**; **triangular**; outer edge: Delhi ridge (NW), **Rajmahal hills (E)**, Gir (W), Cardamom hills (S); extensions: **Meghalaya / Karbi Anglong plateau** and Kutch-Kathiawar.
[35:1:3] - **Tilts east** (most rivers flow east); Narmada and Tapi flow west in rift valleys.
[35:1:4] - NCERT: three broad groups – **Deccan Plateau, Central Highlands, North-Eastern Plateau** (Kutch is not one).
[35:1:5] - **S.P. Chatterjee** divides the Peninsula into 8 parts; the **Mahanadi basin** falls in the **Northern Deccan Plateau** (old app key).
[35:1:6] # Plateaus
[35:1:7] TABLE head: Plateau | Where | Facts
  [35:1:7.0] Malwa | Western MP and SE Rajasthan | Between the Aravalli and the Vindhya (Vindhya to its south); Bundelkhand to its east; lava, black (lava) soil; two drainage systems – to the Arabian Sea (Narmada, Mahi) and to the Bay of Bengal (Chambal, Betwa → Yamuna)
  [35:1:7.1] Chota Nagpur | Mainly Jharkhand; also Chhattisgarh, Odisha, WB, Bihar | Storehouse of minerals, "Ruhr of India", biggest mineral deposits; series of plateaus (patlands: Ranchi, Hazaribagh, Palamu) – "a front sloping" plateau; source of Damodar (Khamarpat hill), Koel, Subarnarekha; Rajmahal hills on its north-eastern edge (Jharkhand)
  [35:1:7.2] Deccan | South of the Narmada; ~7 lakh sq km | Largest plateau; northern boundary Satpura, Mahadeo, Maikal; Western and Eastern Ghats on the sides; Andhra Pradesh lies on the Deccan plateau; Vidarbha is the eastern region of Maharashtra
  [35:1:7.3] Meghalaya (Shillong) | Meghalaya | Part of the Peninsular Plateau, cut off by the Malda (Garo–Rajmahal) gap; Garo, Khasi, Jaintia hills (Bhuban hills of Assam are not part); living root bridges of the Khasis in Meghalaya
  [35:1:7.4] Dandakaranya | Chhattisgarh and Odisha, also Telangana, Maharashtra, AP | ~89,078 sq km; central-eastern highland
  [35:1:7.5] Bhander | MP | Southern part of the Vindhyan scarpland
  [35:1:7.6] Karnataka (Mysore) | Karnataka | Malnad = hilly forested western Karnataka (not AP)
[35:1:8] - **Lowest-lying region of India:** **Kuttanad** (Kerala), about 2 m below sea level.
[35:1:9] # Deccan Traps
[35:1:10] - **Fissure eruptions** of basaltic lava → **solidification of lava**; at the **end of the Cretaceous** (Cretaceous–Eocene), in the **north-west** of the Peninsula.
[35:1:11] - 'Trap' = Swedish for **step**; once ~10 lakh sq km, now ~5 lakh sq km; thickness 3,000 m (west) → 150 m (east); weathers into **regur** (black cotton soil).
[35:1:12] TABLE head: Formation | Age (UPSC 1997)
  [35:1:12.0] Deccan Traps | Cretaceous–Eocene
  [35:1:12.1] Western Ghats | Late Cenozoic
  [35:1:12.2] Aravalli | Pre-Cambrian
  [35:1:12.3] Narmada–Tapti alluvium | Pleistocene
[35:1:13] - **Structural statements:** Meghalaya plateau = extension of the Deccan/Peninsular plateau; Kashmir valley formed in a **synclinorium**; the Gangetic plain in a **foredeep** (all true).
[35:1:14] > Exam angle: oldest region = Peninsular Plateau (CGPSC ×2); Chota Nagpur as the mineral storehouse (×4).
[35:1:15] ~~ Sources: NextGen Indian Geography - APPSC Exams 05 p.5-11; PMF Indian Physical Geography 01 p.73-79; OnlyIAS NCERT Indian Geography 03 p.15-16; Rocket Indian Geography p.109-111; Rocket General Geography p.40; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuttanad; app notes 4:35 (sub 4)
[35:1:16] - **Dalma hills:** near Jamshedpur, **Jharkhand** (Chota Nagpur).
[35:1:17] - **River terraces of the Krishna and Godavari** (like the Narmada–Tapi alluvium) are **Pleistocene** (Quaternary).
## SUB 2 | Central Ranges – Vindhya, Satpura, Maikal, Aravalli and Peaks
[35:2:0] # Ranges
[35:2:1] TABLE head: Range | Facts
  [35:2:1.0] Vindhya | North of the Narmada; an escarpment; separates the Northern Plains from the Peninsula (watershed of Ganga and southern rivers); source of Betwa, Ken, Chambal; continues east as Kaimur (MP, UP, Bihar)
  [35:2:1.1] Satpura | "Seven folds"; between the Narmada and the Tapi (a horst); ~900 km; central India; northern boundary of the Deccan; Dhupgarh highest
  [35:2:1.2] Mahadeo hills | Part of the Satpura (Pachmarhi, MP)
  [35:2:1.3] Maikal | Eastern end of the Satpura (MP–Chhattisgarh); Amarkantak = source of Narmada, Son, Johila; Ramgiri hills (Chhattisgarh) placed in the Maikal (CGPSC key)
  [35:2:1.4] Aravalli | Oldest fold range of India (Delhi to Gujarat, ~800 km); Guru Shikhar highest
  [35:2:1.5] Ajanta | Only in Maharashtra (a range in a single State)
  [35:2:1.6] Satmala, Harishchandra, Balaghat | Maharashtra (spurs of the Western Ghats)
  [35:2:1.7] Mandav hills | Gujarat (Kathiawar) – not Maharashtra
  [35:2:1.8] Garhjat | Odisha
[35:2:2] - **West → east:** **Satpura – Mahadeo – Maikal – Chota Nagpur**; **Barwani – Mahadeo – Maikal**; **Mahadeo – Maikal – Chota Nagpur – Khasi**.
[35:2:3] - **North → south:** **Mahadeo hills – Satpura range – Sahyadri** (UPSC 2004).
[35:2:4] - **Narmada** flows between the **Vindhya (north) and the Satpura (south)**.
[35:2:5] - **UPSC 2014 pairs:** **Mahadeo – Central India** and **Mikir – North-East** are right; Cardamom is not on the Coromandel coast, Kaimur not on the Konkan.
[35:2:6] - The Aravalli is the **oldest**, not the youngest, range; Visakhapatnam and Bhubaneswar lie along the Eastern Ghats belt.
[35:2:7] # Peaks
[35:2:8] TABLE head: Peak | Range / State | Height
  [35:2:8.0] Anamudi | Anaimalai, Kerala – highest of South India | 2,695 m
  [35:2:8.1] Doddabetta | Nilgiris, TN | 2,637 m
  [35:2:8.2] Mullayanagiri | Karnataka | 1,892 m
  [35:2:8.3] Guru Shikhar | Aravalli (Mt Abu), Rajasthan | 1,722 m
  [35:2:8.4] Arma Konda | Eastern Ghats, Andhra Pradesh (highest of AP) | 1,680 m
  [35:2:8.5] Kalsubai | Sahyadri, Maharashtra | 1,646 m
  [35:2:8.6] Mahendragiri | Eastern Ghats, Odisha | ~1,501 m
  [35:2:8.7] Parasnath | Giridih, Jharkhand | ~1,365 m
  [35:2:8.8] Dhupgarh | Satpura (Mahadeo hills, Pachmarhi) – highest of MP | 1,350 m
  [35:2:8.9] Gaurlata | Samri Pat, Chhattisgarh (highest of the State) | —
  [35:2:8.10] Nokrek | Garo hills, Meghalaya | 1,412 m
  [35:2:8.11] Girnar | Extinct volcano, Kathiawar | —
[35:2:9] - Height order (with Himalayan peaks): Nanga Parbat > Kamet > Anamudi > Doddabetta; Doddabetta is far lower than Kamet.
[35:2:10] > Exam angle: "highest peak of South India / the Peninsula" = Anamudi (×7); Dhupgarh = Satpura (×4).

[35:2:12] - **Mukandara hills:** an extension of the Vindhyas in south-east **Rajasthan** (Kota).
## SUB 3 | Coastal Plains
[35:3:0] # Divisions
[35:3:1] TABLE head: Coast | Extent | State / features
  [35:3:1.0] Kachchh–Kathiawar | — | Gujarat; Kachchh built by silt of the Indus; Kathiawar part of the plateau
  [35:3:1.1] Konkan | Daman to Goa (northern part of the west coast) | Maharashtra–Goa; marine erosion – cliffs, shoals, reefs, islands; Janjira, Ratnagiri, Sindhudurg
  [35:3:1.2] Kannad (Kanara) | Goa to Mangaluru – the central stretch between Konkan and Malabar | Karnataka
  [35:3:1.3] Malabar | Mangaluru to Kanyakumari | Kerala; lakes, lagoons, backwaters (kayals) – Vembanad (largest, Kochi port), Ashtamudi; dunes = teris
  [35:3:1.4] Utkal | Subarnarekha to Rushikulya | Odisha; Mahanadi delta
  [35:3:1.5] Northern Circars | Mahanadi to the Krishna | Odisha–AP; Chilika lake (largest brackish lagoon)
  [35:3:1.6] Coromandel | Krishna delta to Cape Comorin (Kanyakumari); Pulicat to Kanyakumari | Tamil Nadu (and southern AP); Buckingham Canal (796 km, Kakinada–Parangipettai); Karaikal
[35:3:2] - **Cape Comorin = Kanyakumari**, where the eastern and western coastal plains meet.
[35:3:3] - **West coast north → south:** Janjira (Raigad) – Sindhudurg – Kannur – Nagercoil.
[35:3:4] - **West coast:** narrow, **submergent**, wetter (more rain), estuaries suit ports. **East coast:** broad, **emergent**, deltas, drier; it grows **more rice** than the west coast (A true, R false – the east coast gets **less** rain).
[35:3:5] - **Gulf of Mannar** (not the Gulf of Khambhat) lies between Tamil Nadu (Nagercoil, Rameswaram) and Sri Lanka; **Gulf of Khambhat** (Gujarat) has the largest tidal energy potential.
[35:3:6] - India's coastline is straight because of **faulting** (Cretaceous–early Tertiary break-up of Gondwana).
[35:3:7] - **Kerala** became India's first fully **digital banking** State (7 Jan 2023) – a CA item asked with the coast.
[35:3:8] # Coastline and lagoons
[35:3:9] - **Coastline: 11,098.81 km** (2023-24 remeasurement by the **National Hydrographic Office and Survey of India**; PIB 4 Dec 2025): **Gujarat 2,340.62 km (1st)**, **Tamil Nadu 1,068.69 km (2nd)**, **Andhra Pradesh 1,053.07 km (3rd)**; old figures 7,516.6 km and AP 973.7 km ("974 km, 2nd"). Islands counted: **1,389**.
[35:3:10] - AP: longest district coast **Srikakulam (~193 km)**.
[35:3:11] - **Pulicat** (AP–TN): 2nd-largest brackish lagoon; **Sriharikota** separates it from the sea. **Kolleru**: once a lagoon, now an **inland freshwater lake between the Godavari and Krishna**.
[35:3:12] > Exam angle: Coromandel (×7) and Buckingham Canal (×2) dominate; Settled fact – AP is now **3rd** in coastline.
[35:3:13] ~~ Sources: NextGen Indian Geography - APPSC Exams 05 p.14, 06 p.1-3; OnlyIAS NCERT Indian Geography 03 p.18; PMF Indian Physical Geography 01 p.82; RUNBOOK settled facts (PIB 2198800, 4 Dec 2025); tribuneindia.com (Kerala digital banking, 7 Jan 2023); app notes 4:35 (sub 7, 8)
[35:3:14] - **Emergent coast:** land rose or the sea fell → wide plains, bars, lagoons, deltas (east coast); **submergent:** drowned valleys, estuaries, rias (west coast).
[35:3:15] - **Western Ghats States (6):** Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu; the Himalayas spread over far more than five States/UTs.
## SUB 4 | Indian Desert and the Rann of Kutch
[35:4:0] # Thar (Great Indian Desert)
[35:4:1] - Lies **north-west / west of the Aravallis**; undulating sandy plain with **barchans and longitudinal (seif) dunes**; rainfall **below 150 mm**; **Marusthali** (true desert, west) and **Bagar** (semi-arid strip along the Aravallis).
[35:4:2] - Order of observation (APPSC key): **semi-arid/arid weather → sand dunes → thorny bushes → seasonal streams** that appear only with rain.
[35:4:3] - Extent: from the edge of the **Rann of Kutch** across the **Luni** to the Aravalli face (APPSC key).
[35:4:4] - **Luni** = the only large river of the region; rises in the **Aravalli near Ajmer**; **"Indian desert" and "Thar desert" are the same desert**; it is **lost in the Rann of Kutch** – does not reach the sea or the Gulf of Kutch.
[35:4:5] - Under the sea in the Mesozoic (Akal wood fossils, Jaisalmer); salt lakes – **Sambhar** largest.
[35:4:6] # Rann of Kutch
[35:4:7] - **Seasonal salt marsh** (Great Rann north, Little Rann south), Gujarat–Sindh; once a shallow arm of the Arabian Sea / Kutch an island; **repeated falls in sea level** left the present marshland (UPSC 2023).
[35:4:8] - **Indian Wild Ass Sanctuary** – Little Rann, **Gujarat**; **Banni grasslands** at the edge of the salt marsh – **Gujarat**.
[35:4:9] - **Agarias** = traditional **salt-pan workers** of the Little Rann, Gujarat (UPSC 2009).
[35:4:10] ~~ Sources: PMF Indian Physical Geography 01 p.69-70; OnlyIAS NCERT Indian Geography 03 p.17; NextGen Indian Geography - APPSC Exams 06 p.2; app notes 4:35 (sub 3)
## SUB 5 | Physiographic Divisions of India
[35:5:0] - **Six divisions** (NCERT): **Himalayas, Northern Plains, Peninsular Plateau, Indian Desert, Coastal Plains, Islands**.
[35:5:1] - **Plains** cover the largest share of land (about **43%**), mountains ~30%, plateaus ~27%.
[35:5:2] - **Oldest** = Peninsular Plateau; **youngest** = Northern Plains (NextGen p.13).
[35:5:3] - Statements: the **Sahara** is **not** in the subcontinent; the **Eastern Ghats** run along the east coast; the **Deccan** is a **basaltic plateau**, not fertile lowland.
[35:5:4] TABLE head: Feature | Description
  [35:5:4.0] Himalaya | World's highest range, peaks over 29,000 ft
  [35:5:4.1] Thar | Arid region of sand dunes and extreme temperatures
  [35:5:4.2] Deccan | High plateau covering much of southern India
  [35:5:4.3] Ganga–Brahmaputra delta | Vast alluvial plain where two great rivers meet
  [35:5:4.4] Chota Nagpur | Central/eastern India, rich in minerals
  [35:5:4.5] Malwa | MP and Rajasthan
  [35:5:4.6] Karnataka plateau | Karnataka, TN, Telangana parts
  [35:5:4.7] Deccan plateau (match) | Southern India, between the Eastern and Western Ghats
[35:5:5] ~~ Sources: OnlyIAS NCERT Indian Geography 03 p.13-14; NextGen Indian Geography - APPSC Exams 04 p.13; app notes 4:35 (sub 1)
## SUB 6 | Northern Plains
[35:6:0] - **Aggradational** plain built by Himalayan rivers (Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra); ~6.5–7 lakh sq km; 2,400–3,200 km long; northern edge = **Himalayan Frontal Fault**; geologically **youngest** division.
[35:6:1] - Very gentle slope: **about 200 m drop over ~1,600 km** from the Yamuna at Delhi to the Bay of Bengal (average plain height ~200 m).
[35:6:2] TABLE head: Belt | Feature
  [35:6:2.0] Bhabar | Pebbles at the Shiwalik foot; streams sink
  [35:6:2.1] Terai | Swampy, marshy, forested belt where streams re-emerge
  [35:6:2.2] Bhangar | Older alluvium, kankar
  [35:6:2.3] Khadar | Newer floodplain alluvium
  [35:6:2.4] Bhur | Undulating aeolian sandy deposit in the upper Ganga–Yamuna doab
[35:6:3] - Punjab plain = doabs of Indus tributaries; Ganga plain divisions: Ganga–Yamuna doab, Rohilkhand, Avadh, Bihar, Bengal (not Malwa); **Kosi** = "Sorrow of Bihar", a mega-fan; Ganga–Brahmaputra delta = deltaic plain; Chambal = ravines/badlands; loess plains = wind-blown silt.
[35:6:4] ~~ Sources: NextGen Indian Geography - APPSC Exams 04 p.13-14, 05 p.2; PMF Indian Physical Geography 01 p.66-68; app notes 4:35 (sub 2)
## SUB 7 | Islands
[35:7:0] TABLE head: Feature | Andaman & Nicobar | Lakshadweep
  [35:7:0.0] Sea | Bay of Bengal, ~1,200 km SE of the mainland | Arabian Sea, off Kerala
  [35:7:0.1] Origin | Elevated submarine mountains (Arakan Yoma extension); volcanic Barren and Narcondam | Coral atolls
  [35:7:0.2] Count | About 572 islands/islets (NCERT); A&N administration counts 836 | 36 islands, 10 inhabited (NCERT summary says 11)
  [35:7:0.3] Area | ~8,249 sq km | ~32 sq km – smallest UT
  [35:7:0.4] Capital | Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair, renamed 2024) | Kavaratti
  [35:7:0.5] Highest | Saddle Peak (~738 m, North Andaman) | Low-lying
  [35:7:0.6] Notes | Jarawa, Sentinelese; Barren Island = only active volcano; Ten Degree Channel (Andaman–Nicobar) | Amindivi group north of 11° N; largest island Andrott; Minicoy southernmost; Nine Degree Channel (Minicoy–rest), Eight Degree Channel (Minicoy–Maldives)
[35:7:1] - Other islands: **Salsette** (Mumbai, Maharashtra), **Divi** (Krishna mouths), **Piram** (Gulf of Khambhat), **Diu** (near the Gulf of Khambhat), Sriharikota (AP).
[35:7:2] ~~ Sources: OnlyIAS NCERT Indian Geography 03 p.18; NextGen Indian Geography - APPSC Exams 06 p.3-5; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lakshadweep (36 islands, 10 inhabited, 32.62 sq km, Andrott largest); app notes 4:35 (sub 9)
[35:7:3] - **Rameswaram (Pamban) island** (Ramanathapuram, TN) lies **between India and Sri Lanka** in the Palk Strait–Gulf of Mannar; **Elephanta** and **Salsette** are near Mumbai.
[35:7:4] - **Tillanchong** is a **Nicobar** island; **Agatti, Kavaratti, Kalpeni, Andrott, Minicoy** are Lakshadweep islands.
[35:7:5] - **Offshore (near-shore) islands:** Bhatkal (Karnataka), Arnala (Maharashtra), Henry (West Bengal) – unlike remote Minicoy.
[35:7:6] - **Salsette** (Mumbai + Thane) = India's **most populous island**; **Majuli** (Assam) = largest river island.
[35:7:7] - **Port Blair (Sri Vijaya Puram)** lies on **South Andaman**; **Duncan Passage** separates South Andaman from Little Andaman.
[35:7:8] - **Great Nicobar** (Indira Point, 6°45′ N) is about **150 km from Sumatra** across the **Great Channel** – the closest foreign land.
[35:7:9] - **PIN codes:** A&N = **744** (zone 7, with WB, Odisha, NE); Lakshadweep = **682** (zone 6, Kerala).
[35:7:10] - **Kavaratti** = capital and **largest town** of Lakshadweep (Census 2011: 11,210, Andrott town 11,191); **Andrott** = largest island by area.
